question: Which two drugs are combined inside a single ampoule of Syntometrine?

options.A: Ergometrine and hydralazine
options.B: Misoprostol and oxytocin
options.C: Oxytocin and ergometrine maleate
options.D: Oxytocin and magnesium sulfate

explanation: Syntometrine is a fixed-dose combination medication containing both oxytocin and ergometrine maleate to manage the third stage of labor. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why are two different drugs mixed together in Syntometrine?

options.A: Both drugs work at the exact same speed to relax the lower uterine segment
options.B: One provides immediate contraction while the other sustains the uterine tone
options.C: It completely eliminates all normal side effects associated with ergot alkaloids
options.D: It allows the medication to be safely taken by mouth instead of injection

explanation: Oxytocin works very fast to start contractions, while ergometrine takes a little longer but keeps the uterus firm over a longer period. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does the ergometrine part of the drug help stop bleeding after birth?

options.A: By relaxing the cervical os to allow rapid passage of lochia
options.B: By lowering the general body temperature to slow down circulation
options.C: By dissolving any blood clots forming inside the uterine cavity
options.D: By causing a sustained tonic contraction that squeezes open blood vessels

explanation: Ergometrine makes the uterine muscle clamp down steadily. This action physically pinches off the open blood vessels where the placenta detached. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h2)

question: What effect can ergometrine have on a patient's blood pressure?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged because the drug targets only the uterus
options.B: It can rise significantly due to widespread blood vessel constriction
options.C: It fluctuates wildly in a rhythmic pattern matching the uterine contractions
options.D: It drops rapidly because blood pools inside the relaxed lower limbs

explanation: Ergometrine narrows blood vessels all over the body, which can cause blood pressure to go up. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h2)

question: When is Syntometrine primarily used in the labor ward?

options.A: Active management of the third stage of labor
options.B: Induction of labor in a post-term pregnancy
options.C: Relief of severe afterpains following delivery
options.D: Softening of an unfavorable cervix before induction

explanation: Syntometrine is given right after the baby is born to help deliver the placenta and prevent heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h3)

question: At what exact point during delivery should a midwife give Syntometrine?

options.A: Four hours before the expected time of delivery to ripen the uterine muscles
options.B: Right after the delivery of the baby's anterior shoulder or newborn infant
options.C: During the latent phase of the first stage of labor to speed up cervical dilation
options.D: Only after manual removal of a retained placenta in the operating theatre

explanation: Giving it as the baby is born ensures it starts working right as the third stage begins. The midwife must first make sure there is no second baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the standard route of administration for a dose of Syntometrine?

options.A: Rectal suppository capsule
options.B: Sublingual absorption tablet
options.C: Intramuscular injection
options.D: Intravenous infusion drip

explanation: Syntometrine is normally given as a single intramuscular injection to provide a steady and safe absorption rate. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is giving Syntometrine directly into a vein (IV bolus) discouraged?

options.A: It takes over thirty minutes to produce any noticeable clinical effect
options.B: It can cause a dangerous and sudden spike in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: It completely stops the oxytocin from working on the uterine muscle fibers
options.D: It causes the placenta to detach before the baby's head is even born

explanation: An intravenous injection of ergometrine causes blood vessels to narrow too quickly, leading to a dangerous spike in blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of these conditions means a patient should NOT receive Syntometrine?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Mild gestational iron deficiency
options.C: Premature rupture of membranes
options.D: Normal uncomplicated multiparity

explanation: Giving Syntometrine to a patient with high blood pressure or preeclampsia is dangerous because it can raise their blood pressure even further. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h5)

question: A midwife is delivering twins. When is it safe to give Syntometrine?

options.A: Only after the second twin has been safely delivered
options.B: Immediately after the first twin's anterior shoulder appears
options.C: During the first stage of labor to speed up twin delivery
options.D: Before delivering either baby to prevent any blood loss

explanation: Syntometrine must never be given while another baby is still inside because strong contractions could harm the remaining twin. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h5)

question: What are two very common side effects after receiving Syntometrine?

options.A: Excessive hair loss and rash
options.B: Lower limb swelling and edema
options.C: Nausea and vomiting
options.D: Severe drowsiness and sleep

explanation: Many patients feel nauseous or vomit shortly after receiving Syntometrine due to how ergot medicines affect the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why do patients often complain of strong cramp-like pains after a Syntometrine injection?

options.A: The drug causes intense, sustained contractions of the uterine muscle fibers
options.B: It forces the pelvic bones to rapidly separate back to pre-pregnancy size
options.C: It strips the inner lining of the stomach causing acute gastric ulcers
options.D: It causes severe dehydration by locking water inside the urinary bladder

explanation: The medicine makes the uterus contract very firmly, which naturally causes strong afterpains in the abdomen. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h6)

question: How should Syntometrine be stored to keep it working properly?

options.A: Submerged in sterile saline solution at body temperature
options.B: Refrigeration between 2°C and 8°C protected from light
options.C: Stored openly at room temperature in the delivery ward
options.D: Kept inside a dark freezer compartment below zero degrees

explanation: Syntometrine spoils easily if exposed to heat and light, so it must be kept in the refrigerator. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is an essential check a midwife must perform after giving Syntometrine?

options.A: Palpating the uterine fundus to ensure it stays firm and contracted
options.B: Checking the newborn's sucking reflex during early breastfeeding
options.C: Measuring hourly urine output to check for renal tube blockage
options.D: Testing the client's visual acuity for signs of permanent blindness

explanation: The main goal of the drug is to keep the uterus hard, so the midwife must regularly feel the abdomen to confirm the uterus is contracted and bleeding is controlled. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h7)

question: What type of natural body chemical is misoprostol designed to copy?

options.A: Oxytocin hormone
options.B: Prostaglandin E1
options.C: Estrogen receptor
options.D: Progesterone steroid

explanation: Misoprostol is manufactured as a synthetic version of prostaglandin E1, which naturally stimulates uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is misoprostol so useful in rural health centers that lack reliable electricity?

options.A: It remains stable at room temperature without strict refrigeration
options.B: It completely replaces the need for any blood transfusion services
options.C: It dissolves completely within seconds in plain cold water
options.D: It can only be given safely by senior medical consultants

explanation: Unlike oxytocin which spoils quickly without a cold chain, misoprostol tolerates ambient heat well, making it ideal for rural settings. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h1)

question: What does misoprostol do to the cervix when helping to start labor?

options.A: Complete calcification of tissue
options.B: Cervical softening and dilation
options.C: Instant closure of the internal os
options.D: Thickening of the mucus plug

explanation: Misoprostol breaks down cervical collagen to help the cervix soften, efface, and open up for delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h2)

question: How do uterine contractions stop heavy bleeding after the baby and placenta are born?

options.A: They permanently freeze the clotting factors in the blood
options.B: They force the kidneys to produce more clotting proteins
options.C: They squeeze the open maternal blood vessels shut
options.D: They lower the mother's overall blood pressure instantly

explanation: Contractions act as natural clamps, pressing down on the open blood vessels in the uterus to stop postpartum bleeding. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which way of giving misoprostol gets it into the bloodstream the fastest?

options.A: Topical skin cream
options.B: Oral swallowing
options.C: Vaginal
options.D: Sublingual

explanation: Dissolving the tablets under the tongue bypasses the liver and allows very fast entry into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h3)

question: A woman is bleeding heavily after childbirth and cannot stop vomiting, so she cannot swallow pills. What alternative way can a midwife give misoprostol?

options.A: Subcutaneous skin puncture
options.B: Intramuscular deep injection
options.C: Rectal
options.D: Intravenous infusion

explanation: The rectal route works very well for postpartum hemorrhage when the patient is vomiting or unable to take medications by mouth. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary obstetric use for misoprostol?

options.A: Prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Treating severe maternal malaria infections
options.C: Lowering high blood glucose levels during pregnancy
options.D: Stopping premature contractions at 24 weeks gestation

explanation: Misoprostol is widely endorsed for preventing and managing excessive bleeding after delivery, especially in low-resource settings. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is misoprostol often used when managing an incomplete miscarriage?

options.A: It assists the uterus in expelling retained tissue without surgery
options.B: It cures underlying bacterial infections in the birth canal
options.C: It permanently prevents any future pregnancies from occurring
options.D: It numbs the pelvic floor muscles to eliminate pain entirely

explanation: Medical management with misoprostol offers a safe, non-surgical option for clearing the uterus after early pregnancy loss. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which patient condition means misoprostol should definitely NOT be used to start labor?

options.A: Previous cesarean section scar on the uterus
options.B: A maternal age greater than thirty-five years
options.C: Mild gestational hypertension without organ damage
options.D: A documented history of mild seasonal allergies

explanation: A scarred uterus from a previous surgery has a high risk of tearing open when exposed to strong prostaglandins like misoprostol. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main danger of giving misoprostol at the same time as other strong contraction-inducing drugs?

options.A: Complete failure of the cervix to ever open up
options.B: Dangerous uterine hyperstimulation and potential rupture
options.C: Severe permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Immediate drop in maternal body temperature to zero

explanation: Combining strong uterine stimulants causes contractions to become too frequent and intense, which can harm both mother and baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which mild, harmless side effect often happens shortly after a patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Sudden loss of hearing ability
options.B: Complete hair loss on the head
options.C: Shivering and mild fever
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eyes

explanation: Temporary shivering and mild chills are common side effects of prostaglandins and usually go away on their own. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)

question: A midwife is monitoring a woman whose labor was started with misoprostol. The midwife notices five strong contractions every ten minutes, and the baby's heart rate is dropping. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Give another dose of misoprostol to speed up delivery
options.B: Notify the doctor immediately about uterine hyperstimulation
options.C: Ignore the finding because it is a normal side effect
options.D: Encourage the mother to walk briskly around the ward

explanation: Too many contractions in a short time frame signal hyperstimulation, which can stress the baby and requires prompt medical attention. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main medical use of nifedipine outside of pregnancy care?

options.A: Stopping postpartum bleeding
options.B: Treating high blood pressure
options.C: Lowering high blood sugar
options.D: Relieving severe morning sickness

explanation: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker, which is a standard medication used to manage high blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do midwives sometimes give nifedipine when a mother goes into very early labor?

options.A: To delay delivery long enough for steroid injections
options.B: To completely prevent any future pregnancy complications
options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix safely
options.D: To permanently stop the labor process until term

explanation: Tocolytic drugs do not stop labor permanently. They help buy a 48-hour window so steroid injections can mature the baby's lungs. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which specific mineral ion is blocked from entering muscle cells by nifedipine?

options.A: Chloride
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Nifedipine is classified as a calcium channel blocker, meaning it stops calcium from entering smooth muscle cells. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does preventing calcium entry help to stop uterine contractions?

options.A: It closes the cervix tightly shut
options.B: It forces the placenta to produce less fluid
options.C: It makes the baby sleep inside the womb
options.D: It keeps the muscle fibers from shortening

explanation: Calcium is needed for muscle fibers to slide together and contract. Without it, the uterine muscle stays relaxed. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h2)

question: Between which weeks of pregnancy is nifedipine used as a tocolytic most often?

options.A: 10 and 20 weeks
options.B: After 42 completed weeks
options.C: 24 and 34 weeks
options.D: 36 and 40 weeks

explanation: This gestational age range is when the fetus is premature enough to benefit from delayed delivery but still viable outside the womb. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using nifedipine during preterm labor?

options.A: Permanently stopping labor until full term is reached
options.B: Buying temporary time for fetal lung maturation
options.C: Curing the underlying infection causing early labor
options.D: Relieving the mother of all lower back pain

explanation: The goal is a short-term delay to allow steroids to work, rather than completely preventing eventual preterm birth. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h3)

question: What type of nifedipine tablet is needed for the first dose in active preterm labor?

options.A: Enteric-coated
options.B: Extended-release
options.C: Immediate-release
options.D: Sustained-release

explanation: Immediate-release tablets are absorbed rapidly to quickly slow down acute uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h4)

question: A patient takes nifedipine for preterm labor, but her contractions continue after the first dose. When is the next loading dose typically given?

options.A: Every 1 to 2 hours
options.B: Every 20 to 30 minutes
options.C: Every 12 hours precisely
options.D: Once every week

explanation: If contractions continue, the loading dose can be repeated at short intervals while monitoring blood pressure closely. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common maternal side effect caused by blood vessels relaxing from nifedipine?

options.A: Sudden swelling of the eyes
options.B: Severe high fever and chills
options.C: Inability to move the legs
options.D: Flushing and headaches

explanation: As blood vessels near the skin relax, it often leads to skin flushing, warmth, and mild throbbing headaches. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why must midwives watch closely for a sharp drop in maternal blood pressure during this therapy?

options.A: It can reduce blood flow through the placenta to the baby
options.B: It stops the kidneys from producing any urine permanently
options.C: It causes the uterine muscle to tear open suddenly
options.D: It makes the mother fall into a deep, unarousable coma

explanation: If maternal blood pressure drops too low, placental blood flow decreases, which can lead to fetal distress. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following conditions means nifedipine should not be given?

options.A: Baseline low blood pressure
options.B: Mild gestational diabetes
options.C: Mild pregnancy-related nausea
options.D: A history of large babies

explanation: Giving a blood pressure-lowering medication to a mother who already has low blood pressure is unsafe. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is giving nifedipine at the same time as magnesium sulfate strongly discouraged?

options.A: It completely stops the baby from breathing at birth
options.B: It causes severe allergic rashes on the skin
options.C: It makes the labor contractions much stronger
options.D: It can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure

explanation: Both medications lower blood pressure, and using them together can cause severe maternal hypotension. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h6)

question: What vital signs must a midwife check immediately before giving every dose of nifedipine?

options.A: Respiratory rate and depth
options.B: Blood pressure and pulse
options.C: Blood sugar level
options.D: Body temperature only

explanation: Checking blood pressure and pulse ensures the mother is not developing low blood pressure or a fast heart rate. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h7)

question: A patient is due for her next maintenance dose of nifedipine, but her blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Wait five minutes and check the temperature
options.B: Withhold the dose and inform the doctor
options.C: Administer the dose with a glass of water
options.D: Double the dose to fix the low pressure

explanation: A systolic blood pressure reading below 90 mmHg is a safety threshold requiring the medication to be held. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary medical use of salbutamol outside of obstetrics?

options.A: Preventing postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Relieving airway constriction in asthma
options.C: Speeding up labor contractions
options.D: Lowering high blood pressure in pregnancy

explanation: Salbutamol is a well-known bronchodilator used mainly to open up the airways in patients suffering from asthma attacks. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why would a midwife administer a tocolytic agent like salbutamol during preterm labor?

options.A: To kill any bacterial infections causing the early labor
options.B: To temporarily stop uterine contractions and delay delivery
options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix for a faster birth
options.D: To strengthen the contractions so the baby comes out quicker

explanation: Tocolytics relax the uterine muscle to slow down or halt premature labor, giving time for protective treatments like steroids to work. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which specific body receptor does salbutamol target to relax the muscles?

options.A: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
options.B: Beta-2 adrenergic receptors
options.C: Oxytocin receptors
options.D: Alpha-1 adrenergic receptors

explanation: Salbutamol specifically targets beta-2 receptors, which are abundant in smooth muscle tissue found in the airways and the uterus. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h2)

question: How does lowering calcium inside the muscle cells cause the uterus to relax?

options.A: Calcium is needed for muscle fibers to slide together and contract
options.B: Calcium stops the baby from moving around inside the womb
options.C: Calcium prevents the uterus from receiving blood from the placenta
options.D: Calcium makes the muscle cells destroy themselves quickly

explanation: Calcium acts as the key trigger for muscle contraction; removing it keeps the muscle fibers relaxed and stops them from squeezing. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h2)

question: A woman at 30 weeks gestation is having frequent contractions at a rural clinic. Why is salbutamol given to her?

options.A: To make sure she delivers her baby vaginally instead of by surgery
options.B: To permanently cure her risk of having another early labor
options.C: To help her placenta grow larger before the baby arrives
options.D: To delay birth long enough to transfer her to a better equipped hospital

explanation: Short-term tocolysis buys time to move a vulnerable mother and baby to a facility that can handle preterm newborns. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the typical maximum duration for using salbutamol as a tocolytic?

options.A: Nine months
options.B: Two full weeks
options.C: About 48 hours
options.D: Until the end of the first trimester

explanation: Salbutamol is only used short-term (roughly 48 hours) because the body quickly builds a tolerance to its relaxing effects. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which method of giving medication is commonly used for acute tocolytic therapy in an emergency?

options.A: Intravenous infusion
options.B: Subcutaneous injection
options.C: Topical skin patch
options.D: Intramuscular depot

explanation: Intravenous delivery allows rapid control and easy adjustment of the dose when stopping acute contractions urgently. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why must midwives calculate and monitor salbutamol dosages very carefully?

options.A: The medication is extremely expensive to waste in the ward
options.B: Higher doses will make the baby grow too large for a normal birth
options.C: Small mistakes can easily cause dangerous heart problems for the mother
options.D: The drug loses its color if mixed with the wrong type of fluid

explanation: Because salbutamol stimulates beta receptors throughout the body, incorrect dosing heavily strains the maternal cardiovascular system. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h4)

question: What maternal vital sign is most critical to track closely during salbutamol therapy?

options.A: Body temperature
options.B: Blood glucose level
options.C: Pulse rate
options.D: Urine output

explanation: Salbutamol frequently causes rapid heart rate (tachycardia), making pulse monitoring essential to prevent cardiac stress. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h5)

question: A patient receiving a salbutamol infusion suddenly has a pulse rate of 130 beats per minute. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Reduce or stop the infusion and notify the doctor
options.B: Administer a painkiller for a headache
options.C: Increase the drip rate to flush the drug out faster
options.D: Give her a cold drink of water and tell her to relax

explanation: A heart rate above safe limits means the drug dose is too high, requiring an immediate reduction or halt to protect the mother's heart. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of salbutamol therapy?

options.A: Fine tremors in the hands
options.B: Fast pounding heartbeat
options.C: Severe slowing of the heart rate
options.D: High blood sugar levels

explanation: Salbutamol speeds up the heart (tachycardia) rather than slowing it down. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why are pregnant women receiving salbutamol at a higher risk for developing pulmonary edema?

options.A: Lungs stop working normally whenever uterine contractions are forced to stop
options.B: The drug causes fluid shifts and cardiovascular strain, sometimes worsened by other drugs like steroids
options.C: Pregnant women naturally drink too much water while staying in the hospital ward
options.D: The medication directly damages the tiny air sacs in the mother's lungs

explanation: Cardiovascular changes from beta-agonists combined with fluid overload or steroid use can cause fluid to leak into the lungs. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h6)

question: A woman at 32 weeks is having contractions, but her temperature is high and her membranes have been ruptured for three days with foul discharge. Why is salbutamol contraindicated?

options.A: Infection makes the mother's heart immune to the drug's effects
options.B: Stopping an infected uterus from emptying puts the mother at severe risk
options.C: Fever completely destroys the chemical makeup of salbutamol
options.D: Salbutamol stops antibiotics from working inside the mother's bloodstream

explanation: When chorioamnionitis is present, the priority is delivering the baby to clear the infection, not holding the pregnancy inside. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which medical condition is a major contraindication for receiving salbutamol?

options.A: Significant maternal heart disease
options.B: Uncomplicated gestational diabetes
options.C: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: A history of morning sickness

explanation: Salbutamol places heavy demands on the heart, making it dangerous for women with pre-existing cardiac conditions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which mineral does magnesium sulfate block to help relax the uterus?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Chloride
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Magnesium blocks calcium channels to stop the muscle fibers in the uterus from tightening up. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why do midwives give magnesium sulfate during preterm labor?

options.A: To briefly delay delivery so critical care can be given
options.B: To cure high blood pressure permanently
options.C: To speed up cervical dilation
options.D: To stop menstrual cycles

explanation: Magnesium sulfate buys precious time to give medications that help the baby's lungs mature before birth. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main reason midwives use magnesium sulfate to prevent seizures in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Eclampsia
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the standard medicine used to prevent and manage seizures linked to eclampsia. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h2)

question: A 28-week pregnant woman arrives with high blood pressure, a bad headache, and hyperactive reflexes. What is the priority action?

options.A: Give strong oxytocin infusion to induce labor
options.B: Administer magnesium sulfate to prevent seizures
options.C: Prepare for an immediate home discharge
options.D: Start oral iron supplements for anemia

explanation: Signs of severe pre-eclampsia require prompt magnesium sulfate to stop the condition from progressing to full seizures. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h2)

question: How is the starting loading dose of magnesium sulfate usually given?

options.A: Rubbed onto the skin as a cream
options.B: Injected into deep muscle all at once
options.C: Swallowed as a single tablet
options.D: Infused slowly over a short period

explanation: The loading dose is given over 15 to 20 minutes to quickly build up the right level in the blood. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is a continuous maintenance infusion given after the initial loading dose of magnesium sulfate?

options.A: To stimulate milk production
options.B: To flush toxins from the liver
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure to zero
options.D: To keep blood levels stable and prevent contractions

explanation: The body clears magnesium quickly, so a steady drip keeps the medication level high enough to work. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the minimum hourly urine output needed for a patient on magnesium sulfate?

options.A: 30 milliliters per hour
options.B: 250 milliliters per hour
options.C: 10 milliliters per hour
options.D: 100 milliliters per hour

explanation: Making at least 30 ml of urine per hour shows the kidneys are clearing the drug and preventing buildup. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which sign usually disappears first when a patient's magnesium sulfate level gets too high?

options.A: Spontaneous eye blinking
options.B: Deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Normal body temperature
options.D: Regular bowel sounds

explanation: Knee-jerk reflexes slow down and disappear before breathing problems or other serious signs of toxicity occur. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the specific emergency antidote used to reverse magnesium sulfate toxicity?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Sodium bicarbonate
options.C: Oxytocin injection
options.D: Vitamin K ampoule

explanation: Calcium gluconate counteracts the relaxing effects of too much magnesium on the muscles and breathing. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h5)

question: A patient on magnesium sulfate has a slow breathing rate of 8 breaths per minute and missing knee reflexes. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion immediately
options.B: Wait for the doctor to finish out-patient clinic
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.D: Increase the infusion rate

explanation: Stopping the medication is always the first step when signs of toxicity appear, before giving any rescue drugs. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which local tissue messengers help soften the cervix and start uterine contractions?

options.A: Prolactin and cortisol
options.B: Prostaglandins E2 and F2 alpha
options.C: Oxytocin and vasopressin
options.D: Estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Prostaglandins E2 and F2 alpha are produced locally in reproductive tissues to help the cervix ripen and prepare the uterus for contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why are synthetic prostaglandins usually placed directly into the vagina or cervix instead of being swallowed as regular pills?

options.A: Pills take too long to dissolve in the stomach fluids of pregnant women
options.B: Oral tablets cause severe damage to the lining of the human stomach
options.C: They break down very quickly near where they are made in local tissues
options.D: Direct application prevents the liver from filtering out the active drug

explanation: Prostaglandins have a very short lifespan in the body, so placing them right at the target organ ensures they work effectively before they degrade. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h1)

question: What scoring system do midwives commonly use to check if a cervix is ready and favorable before inducing labor?

options.A: Apgar score
options.B: Glasgow coma scale
options.C: Bish Butler scale
options.D: Bishop score

explanation: The Bishop score looks at dilation, effacement, station, consistency, and position to see if the cervix is ready for labor. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h2)

question: How do prostaglandins physically change a firm, unripe cervix to make it soft?

options.A: They stimulate the local production of heavy scar tissue to widen the canal
options.B: They cause the muscular walls of the cervix to contract tightly until it opens
options.C: They dry out the cervical tissues to make them brittle and easy to tear
options.D: They break down rigid collagen and increase water retention in the tissue

explanation: Prostaglandins break down tough collagen fibers and pull water into the tissue, which makes the cervix soft and ready for delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main goal of using prostaglandins when labor needs to be started artificially in the hospital?

options.A: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: To relieve severe labor pain without using regional anesthesia
options.C: To soften and prepare an unfavorable cervix for delivery
options.D: To completely stop all uterine activity during preterm labor

explanation: Prostaglandins are primarily used when the cervix is still firm and closed, helping to prepare it before active labor begins. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h3)

question: A woman at 41 weeks of pregnancy is admitted for induction with a Bishop score of three. What is the best first step?

options.A: Start an immediate high-dose oxytocin intravenous infusion
options.B: Perform an emergency primary cesarean section right away
options.C: Send the patient home to wait for spontaneous labor to start
options.D: Administer a cervical ripening agent like prostaglandin

explanation: A Bishop score of three is low and means the cervix is unfavorable. Using a ripening agent helps prepare the cervix before moving on to oxytocin. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which medication was originally made for stomach ulcers but is now widely used for cervical ripening?

options.A: Methylergometrine
options.B: Carboprost
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Dinoprostone

explanation: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin medication that is affordable and holds up well in warm climates, making it popular for labor induction. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of a dinoprostone vaginal insert over misoprostol tablets during labor induction?

options.A: It costs significantly less money for patients in low-resource clinics
options.B: It never causes any side effects related to stomach upset or fever
options.C: It remains completely stable even in very hot tropical climates without refrigeration
options.D: It can be physically removed from the vagina if uterine overactivity occurs

explanation: The dinoprostone insert has a retrieval string attached, allowing a midwife to pull it out easily if the uterus starts contracting too frequently. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the standard recommended starting dose of misoprostol when placed in the vagina for cervical ripening?

options.A: 500 micrograms
options.B: 50 milligrams
options.C: 200 milligrams
options.D: 25 micrograms

explanation: Starting with a low dose of 25 micrograms helps prevent sudden, overly strong contractions and keeps the process safe. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why must midwives be very careful with standard commercial misoprostol tablets found in general hospital pharmacies?

options.A: Oral tablets will dissolve instantly upon contact with any vaginal moisture
options.B: The drug manufacturer strictly forbids its use by midwives in maternity wards
options.C: Tablets meant for ulcers contain doses that are far too high for safe labor induction
options.D: The medication loses all of its chemical potency within ten minutes of exposure to air

explanation: Stomach ulcer tablets usually come in 200-microgram doses, which are much too strong for induction and can cause dangerous complications if not properly divided. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h5)

question: What assessment should a midwife always perform right BEFORE giving a cervical ripening prostaglandin?

options.A: Administer a prophylactic dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Insert a large-bore intravenous line for rapid fluid loading
options.C: Confirm a reassuring fetal heart rate pattern
options.D: Perform an artificial rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Checking the baby's heart rate first ensures the baby is doing well before introducing a medicine that changes uterine activity. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why is fetal heart monitoring required for a period right after a prostaglandin insert is placed?

options.A: To measure the exact internal temperature of the amniotic fluid pocket
options.B: To prove to the hospital insurance company that the medication was given correctly
options.C: To speed up the physical softening of the maternal cervix through electrical waves
options.D: To catch sudden changes in fetal heart rate caused by unexpected uterine contractions

explanation: Close monitoring ensures that if the medication causes the uterus to contract too rapidly, the healthcare team can spot and address it quickly. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to avoid using prostaglandins for labor induction?

options.A: A previous classical uterine scar from past surgery
options.B: A history of a low-risk appendectomy in childhood
options.C: Known maternal allergy to prostaglandin medications
options.D: Complete placenta previa blocking the cervical os

explanation: Removing an appendix is a general abdominal surgery that does not affect the uterus, unlike a vertical uterine scar which carries a high risk of tearing. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why does a history of a previous vertical (classical) cesarean section mean prostaglandins should not be used?

options.A: The vertical upper uterine scar has a very high risk of tearing apart under strong contractions
options.B: The muscular wall becomes completely paralyzed and will never contract again
options.C: Prostaglandins interact dangerously with old scar tissue and cause permanent nerve damage
options.D: The previous surgical incision prevents the cervix from ever producing any collagen

explanation: Vertical scars in the upper part of the uterus are weak points that can easily rupture when powerful labor medications are introduced. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h7)

question: How is uterine tachysystole defined during labor induction monitoring?

options.A: Contractions lasting continuously for over fifteen minutes without a break
options.B: Fewer than two contractions in a full twenty-minute observation window
options.C: More than five contractions in ten minutes averaged over thirty minutes
options.D: Painful uterine cramping that occurs only once every hour during the night

explanation: Tachysystole means having too many contractions in a short time, which can lower blood flow to the placenta and stress the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)

question: A patient having labor induced with misoprostol develops six contractions in ten minutes, and the fetal monitor shows late decelerations. What is the midwife's first action?

options.A: Document the findings and wait another thirty minutes to see if it stops
options.B: Turn the patient to her left side and apply oxygen
options.C: Administer a dose of synthetic oxytocin to regularize the rhythm
options.D: Encourage the woman to push hard with the next contraction

explanation: Helping the mother lie on her side and giving oxygen improves blood flow to the placenta and helps relieve stress on the baby during too many contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which main receptor does pethidine target in the central nervous system to relieve pain?

options.A: GABA-A receptor
options.B: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor
options.C: Mu-opioid receptor
options.D: Beta-adrenergic receptor

explanation: Pethidine works primarily by binding to mu-opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord to block pain signals. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h1)

question: How does pethidine's effect on smooth muscle differ from standard morphine?

options.A: It has mild anticholinergic properties that reduce smooth muscle spasm.
options.B: It stimulates excessive contractions by binding to oxytocin sites.
options.C: It causes complete paralysis of all uterine smooth muscle fibers.
options.D: It completely blocks all autonomic nervous system functions.

explanation: Pethidine has weak anticholinergic actions, which means it tends to cause less smooth muscle spasm compared to traditional opiates. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h1)

question: During which phase of labor is pethidine most commonly given?

options.A: Latent phase before true labor
options.B: Immediate postpartum period
options.C: Third stage of labor
options.D: First stage of labor

explanation: Pethidine is typically administered during the active first stage of labor to help mothers manage strong contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h2)

question: A woman at 8 cm dilation asks for pethidine. What is the best clinical response?

options.A: Withhold pethidine because delivery is too close, risking respiratory depression in the baby.
options.B: Give the standard dose intravenously since she is in active transition.
options.C: Combine pethidine with high-flow oxygen to prevent any fetal side effects.
options.D: Administer a double dose immediately to ensure rapid pain relief before she pushes.

explanation: Giving pethidine very close to delivery can cause high drug levels in the newborn, leading to breathing difficulties at birth. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the usual adult dose range for intramuscular pethidine during labor?

options.A: 1 to 2 grams
options.B: 200 to 500 mg
options.C: 50 to 100 mg
options.D: 5 to 10 mg

explanation: Standard guidelines recommend an intramuscular dose of 50 to 100 mg to safely and effectively relieve pain in laboring women. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why does pethidine act faster when given intravenously compared to intramuscularly?

options.A: Intravenous injection bypasses the liver completely on the first pass.
options.B: The volume of fluid injected forces the drug to the brain instantly.
options.C: It triggers a faster release of natural endorphins in the spinal cord.
options.D: The drug enters the bloodstream directly without needing absorption time from muscle tissue.

explanation: Injecting medication straight into a vein skips the time it takes for muscle tissue to absorb the drug. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common maternal side effect of pethidine?

options.A: Drowsiness and sedation
options.B: Delayed gastric emptying
options.C: Nausea and vomiting
options.D: Persistent hypertension

explanation: Pethidine commonly causes sedation and nausea, but persistent high blood pressure is not a direct side effect. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why can pethidine use in labor lead to breathing difficulties in the newborn?

options.A: It forces the baby to take breaths too early while still inside the uterus.
options.B: It causes the umbilical cord to constrict and cut off oxygen supply.
options.C: The drug crosses the placenta and depresses the respiratory center in the fetal brain.
options.D: It completely blocks the transfer of carbon dioxide from the baby's lungs.

explanation: Opioids cross the placenta easily and can slow down the baby's central nervous system, affecting breathing at birth. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which specific drug reverses the breathing depression caused by pethidine?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist used to quickly reverse breathing depression caused by medications like pethidine. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h5)

question: A baby is born breathing very slowly thirty minutes after the mother received IV pethidine. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Provide airway support and ventilation while preparing to administer naloxone.
options.B: Wait for twenty minutes to see if the baby starts crying on its own.
options.C: Give the mother an extra dose of oxytocin to speed up uterine recovery.
options.D: Administer a warm bath to stimulate the newborn's nervous system.

explanation: Providing basic respiratory support and using naloxone to reverse the opioid effect are the critical first steps. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary route by which systemic opioids reach the central nervous system of a laboring woman?

options.A: Spreading via the cerebrospinal fluid pathways
options.B: Absorbing directly through the amniotic fluid
options.C: Traveling through the maternal bloodstream
options.D: Absorbing through the muscles of the cervix

explanation: Systemic medications are absorbed into the mother's blood circulation, which carries the drug to the brain and spinal cord to reduce pain perception. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do systemic opioids remain widely used for labor pain relief across many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: They completely eliminate all labor contractions.
options.B: They prevent the need for any fetal heart monitoring.
options.C: They are more accessible than regional anesthesia.
options.D: They guarantee a shorter duration of the first stage.

explanation: Complex regional techniques require specialized equipment and personnel, making systemic drugs the practical choice in most standard maternity units. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which specific receptors in the central nervous system does morphine primarily bind to?

options.A: Mu-opioid receptors
options.B: Alpha-cholinergic pathways
options.C: Gamma-aminobutyric nodes
options.D: Beta-adrenergic sites

explanation: Morphine exerts its strong pain-relieving effects by targeting and activating mu-opioid receptors within the central nervous system. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h2)

question: How does morphine manage to reach the unborn baby after maternal administration?

options.A: By absorbing via the maternal skin pores
options.B: By crossing the placental barrier
options.C: By diffusing directly through the amniotic sac
options.D: By traveling through the fallopian tubes

explanation: Because of its chemical properties, morphine readily passes from the mother's blood vessels through the placenta into the fetal circulation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is a common standard intramuscular dose of morphine given for pain relief during labor?

options.A: 500 mg
options.B: 50 mg
options.C: 10 mg
options.D: 100 mg

explanation: Ten milligrams given intramuscularly is the standard baseline adult dose for managing moderate to severe labor pain in clinical practice. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h3)

question: A woman is admitted in early latent labor at 2 cm dilation requesting immediate pain relief with morphine. What is the most appropriate action for the midwife?

options.A: Delay administration because giving it too early can slow down labor progress.
options.B: Transfer her straight to the operating theatre for an emergency caesarean section.
options.C: Refuse all forms of pain relief until she reaches full 10 cm dilation.
options.D: Administer a double intravenous dose immediately to speed up her dilation.

explanation: Giving systemic opioids during the latent phase before active labor is established can interfere with uterine contractions and prolong labor. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of morphine for the mother?

options.A: Persistent tachycardia
options.B: Delayed gastric emptying
options.C: Nausea and vomiting
options.D: Excessive drowsiness

explanation: Morphine typically causes sedation and respiratory suppression rather than persistent high heart rates (tachycardia). [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is a baby born shortly after peak maternal morphine administration at high risk for breathing difficulties?

options.A: The umbilical cord wraps tightly around the baby's neck due to sedation.
options.B: The infant develops an immediate allergic reaction to the opioid molecules.
options.C: The drug remains active in the newborn's circulation and suppresses the respiratory center.
options.D: The baby experiences severe dehydration from the mother's delayed gastric emptying.

explanation: Opioids cross the placenta and can depress the baby's breathing drive if delivery happens before the drug is metabolized. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the most critical vital sign to monitor closely after administering morphine to a laboring woman?

options.A: Body temperature
options.B: Blood glucose level
options.C: Capillary refill time
options.D: Respiratory rate

explanation: Monitoring breathing frequency is essential because opioid toxicity directly depresses the respiratory center in the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h5)

question: A laboring patient who received intramuscular morphine 1 hour ago now has a respiratory rate of 10 breaths per minute and is difficult to rouse. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if her breathing rate returns to normal on its own.
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to shake off the sleepiness.
options.C: Call for emergency assistance and prepare the antidote and resuscitation gear.
options.D: Administer an extra dose of oral paracetamol to help with her overall comfort.

explanation: A respiratory rate under 12 breaths per minute with heavy sedation indicates opioid toxicity requiring prompt medical intervention. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which medication acts as the specific antagonist to reverse the effects of morphine?

options.A: Hydralazine
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Naloxone binds to opioid receptors and displaces morphine, quickly reversing central nervous system and respiratory depression. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h6)

question: What should be the immediate primary action when a newborn baby is delivered with severe breathing depression following maternal opioid use?

options.A: Apply warm compresses to the infant's abdomen.
options.B: Encourage immediate breastfeeding in the theatre.
options.C: Provide positive pressure ventilation with oxygen.
options.D: Inject high-dose intravenous glucose immediately.

explanation: Establishing effective lung inflation and oxygenation via bag-valve-mask takes precedence over pharmacological reversal in neonatal resuscitation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h6)

question: At what stage of labor is tramadol usually given to help with pain?

options.A: During the first stage of labor
options.B: Throughout the active pushing phase
options.C: Immediately after placental delivery
options.D: Prior to elective cesarean section

explanation: Tramadol is typically given during the first stage of labor to help the mother cope with progressive contractions before full dilatation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of giving tramadol to a woman in active labor?

options.A: To completely eliminate all physical sensations of labor
options.B: To reduce the intensity of pain to a manageable level
options.C: To relax the pelvic floor muscles completely for delivery
options.D: To speed up cervical dilatation and shorten labor duration

explanation: Systemic analgesics in labor aim to take the edge off contractions and help the mother rest, rather than produce complete numbness. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h1)

question: Besides acting on opioid receptors, which two chemical messengers in the nervous system are affected by tramadol?

options.A: Adrenaline and cortisol
options.B: GABA and histamine
options.C: Serotonin and norepinephrine
options.D: Acetylcholine and dopamine

explanation: Tramadol works by binding to opioid receptors and also blocking the reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine in the central nervous system. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which method of giving tramadol during labor works the fastest?

options.A: Intramuscular
options.B: Oral tablet
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Intravenous

explanation: Giving tramadol directly into the vein provides the quickest onset of action compared to other routes. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h3)

question: A laboring woman receives an intramuscular injection of tramadol. About how long does it take to reach its peak effect?

options.A: 30 to 45 minutes
options.B: 2 to 3 hours
options.C: 5 to 10 minutes
options.D: 6 to 8 hours

explanation: Intramuscular injections take longer to absorb into the bloodstream than intravenous routes, usually showing peak effects around 30 to 45 minutes. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common side effect a mother might feel after taking tramadol?

options.A: Nausea and dizziness
options.B: Severe hypertension
options.C: Rapid hair loss
options.D: Permanent vision loss

explanation: Tramadol frequently causes gastrointestinal and vestibular side effects like nausea, vomiting, and dizziness in laboring mothers. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is becoming too sleepy from tramadol a concern during the second stage of labor?

options.A: It makes it hard for the mother to push effectively when instructed
options.B: It permanently stops the production of natural oxytocin
options.C: It immediately triggers an emergency cesarean section
options.D: It causes the placenta to detach prematurely from the uterine wall

explanation: If a mother is overly drowsy from opioid analgesics, she may struggle to follow pushing directions during the second stage of labor. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a known effect on the newborn if the mother receives tramadol close to delivery?

options.A: Respiratory depression
options.B: Persistent tachycardia
options.C: Premature tooth eruption
options.D: Excessive weight gain

explanation: Opioids crossing the placenta can depress the newborn's respiratory center, leading to slow or shallow breathing at birth. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why must a midwife check newborn resuscitation equipment before a laboring woman receives tramadol?

options.C: To treat maternal postpartum hemorrhage if it occurs

question: Taking tramadol along with which type of drug carries a major risk of dangerous serotonin syndrome?

options.D: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs)

question: Which of the following is NOT a correct responsibility when caring for a patient receiving tramadol during labor?

options.D: Documenting the exact time, route, and dosage of the administered drug

explanation: Leaving a patient unmonitored after giving a central nervous system depressant is unsafe; regular observation is always required. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main use of naloxone in the labor ward?

options.A: To induce maternal sleep during labor
options.B: To speed up active labor contractions
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: To reverse the effects of opioid medications

question: Why must midwives know if a baby's breathing trouble is caused by an opioid or another problem?

options.A: Because other causes require immediate surgical intervention
options.B: Because naloxone only works on respiratory depression caused by opioids
options.C: Because non-opioid depression causes rapid maternal bleeding
options.D: Because opioid drugs must never be given in a standard labor ward

explanation: Naloxone will not help a baby whose breathing problems are caused by a lack of oxygen from a cord problem or other non-opioid issues. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which specific receptors in the body does naloxone attach to?

options.A: Mu-opioid receptors
options.B: Adrenaline receptors
options.C: Oxytocin receptors
options.D: Prostaglandin receptors

explanation: Naloxone attaches to mu-opioid receptors to block narcotic drugs from working. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h2)

question: What can happen if naloxone wears off while an opioid is still active in the body?

options.A: The respiratory depression may return
options.B: The baby will develop an immediate allergy
options.C: The maternal blood pressure will drop permanently
options.D: The placenta will absorb the remaining drug

explanation: Naloxone leaves the body faster than many strong opioids, so breathing can slow down again if the patient is not watched closely. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the standard starting dose of naloxone for a newborn, based on weight?

options.A: 0.01 milligrams
options.B: 10.0 milligrams
options.C: 1.0 milligrams
options.D: 5.0 milligrams

question: A newborn is limp and not breathing after the mother received pethidine. What is the first priority before giving naloxone?

options.A: Establishing an intravenous line in the scalp
options.B: Establishing effective ventilation with a bag and mask
options.C: Waiting twenty minutes to see if the baby cries
options.D: Administering high-flow maternal oxygen

explanation: Clearing the airway and helping the baby breathe with a bag and mask is always done before giving medications during resuscitation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why should naloxone be given slowly and in small doses to a mother in pain?

options.A: To prevent the baby from absorbing any of the antidote
options.B: To stop the uterus from contracting too strongly
options.C: To prevent a sudden surge of severe pain and high blood pressure
options.D: To ensure the drug lasts for the entire duration of labor

explanation: Reversing pain relief too quickly causes sudden severe pain and strains the cardiovascular system. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe practice when giving naloxone to a mother?

options.A: Monitoring maternal blood pressure continuously
options.B: Titrating the medication in small measured amounts
options.C: Injecting the entire emergency dose rapidly all at once
options.D: Preparing for sudden severe withdrawal discomfort

explanation: Giving a large dose all at once takes away pain relief instantly and strains the mother's heart. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h4)

question: What reaction does naloxone cause in a patient who depends on opioids?

options.A: Acute withdrawal syndrome
options.B: Permanent nerve damage
options.C: Immediate deep sleep
options.D: Complete memory loss

explanation: Blocking opioid receptors instantly in a dependent person triggers withdrawal symptoms. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is care needed when considering naloxone for a baby born to a mother with a known opioid addiction?

options.A: It can provoke severe seizures and dangerous withdrawal
options.B: It causes immediate jaundice in the first hour
options.C: It prevents the infant from ever breastfeeding
options.D: It will completely stop the baby's heart permanently

explanation: Blocking opioids suddenly in an addicted newborn can cause dangerous withdrawal signs like seizures. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h5)

question: How long should a midwife monitor a patient after giving naloxone?

options.A: Until the placenta is delivered
options.B: Only for ten minutes
options.C: Until the end of the week
options.D: At least two hours

explanation: Because naloxone wears off quickly, monitoring the patient for at least two hours helps catch any return of breathing problems. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h6)

question: A newborn revived with naloxone forty minutes ago starts breathing slowly again. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The delivery room temperature is too low
options.B: The umbilical cord was clamped too early
options.C: The initial dose of naloxone has worn off
options.D: The baby is experiencing normal newborn sleep

explanation: Naloxone has a short action time, so the longer-acting opioid can start slowing the breathing down again after the antidote wears off. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which two gases are mixed inside an Entonox cylinder?

options.A: Nitrogen and nitrous oxide
options.B: Nitrous oxide and oxygen
options.C: Oxygen and compressed air
options.D: Carbon dioxide and oxygen

question: Why does Entonox contain 50% oxygen alongside the nitrous oxide?

options.A: To make the cylinder lighter
options.B: To speed up the onset of contractions
options.C: To prevent the mother and baby from lacking oxygen
options.D: To give the gas a pleasant smell

explanation: The high oxygen concentration ensures both the mother and the baby get enough oxygen while using the gas. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h1)

question: What safety feature prevents attaching the wrong gas cylinder to an Entonox regulator?

options.A: The pressure release valve
options.B: The flow meter dial
options.C: The pin-index system
options.D: The humidifying chamber

explanation: The pin-index safety system uses specific pin and hole patterns to ensure only the correct cylinder connects to the equipment. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h2)

question: An Entonox cylinder is stored in a very cold room overnight. What is the main risk if it is used immediately?

options.A: The plastic tubing will melt under high pressure
options.B: The demand valve will stop releasing gas completely
options.C: The cylinder will trigger a fire alarm
options.D: The gases inside may separate and deliver uneven concentrations

question: When should a laboring woman start breathing in Entonox during a contraction?

options.A: Only when the midwife says the contraction is over
options.B: At the very first sign that a contraction is starting
options.C: Continuously throughout the first stage of labor
options.D: After the contraction has reached its peak

question: Why is Entonox considered a self-administered pain relief method?

options.A: The machine senses when the uterus tightens
options.B: The mother holds her own mask and the valve opens only when she breathes in
options.C: The woman adjusts the dosage knob on the machine herself
options.D: The midwife leaves the room so the woman manages the tank alone

question: Which vital signs are most important to watch in a woman using Entonox?

options.A: Daily weight and fluid balance
options.B: Fasting blood glucose levels
options.C: Pupil reaction to light
options.D: Respiratory rate and level of consciousness

question: Why is good room ventilation important when Entonox is used often in a labor ward?

options.A: To prevent staff and mothers from breathing in leaked waste gases
options.B: To dry up sweat during the second stage of labor
options.C: To keep the oxygen tanks from overheating
options.D: To ensure the fetal monitor picks up clear signals

explanation: Exhaled nitrous oxide can build up in closed spaces, causing dizziness and fatigue for staff and patients in the unit. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of Entonox during childbirth?

options.A: It puts the mother into a deep sleep during delivery
options.B: It leaves the body very quickly once the mask is removed
options.C: It completely blocks all pain in the lower body
options.D: It requires no breathing technique from the woman

question: What is NOT a typical limitation of Entonox?

options.B: It provides permanent relief that lasts for days after birth
options.C: It offers only mild to moderate pain relief
options.D: It requires coordinated breathing during contractions

question: What should a midwife do first if a laboring woman feels dizzy and confused from using Entonox?

options.A: Administer an intravenous sedative right away

options.C: Position the woman flat on her back without a pillow
options.D: Increase the gas flow rate to maximum pressure

explanation: Taking away the mask allows the nitrous oxide to clear rapidly from the bloodstream, relieving dizziness and confusion quickly. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why might some women experience a dry mouth or mild tingling while using Entonox?

options.A: These are common temporary side effects of breathing the gas mixture
options.B: They mean the blood pressure has risen dangerously
options.C: They show the mother is allergic to oxygen
options.D: They indicate that the baby is in severe distress

question: What type of drug is lignocaine?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory
options.B: Opioid receptor agonist
options.C: Amino-amide local anaesthetic
options.D: Esters of benzoic acid

question: Why do midwives in busy maternity units rely heavily on lignocaine?

options.A: It has a rapid onset and reliably manages perineal pain

options.C: It permanently relaxes the uterine muscles during labour
options.D: It acts as a strong antibiotic against postpartum infections

explanation: Lignocaine works quickly to numb local tissue, making it very helpful for pain relief during perineal repairs and episiotomies. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T6#BMP213_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does lignocaine stop pain signals from traveling along a nerve?

options.A: Stimulating local opioid receptors to block pain perception

options.C: Destroying the myelin sheath surrounding the nerve fibre
options.D: Blocking sodium channels to prevent nerve depolarisation

question: Why is adrenaline sometimes added to a lignocaine solution?

options.A: To prevent allergic skin reactions at the injection site

question: What is the maximum safe dose of plain lignocaine for an adult without adrenaline?

question: Why should a midwife pull back on the syringe plunger before injecting lignocaine?

question: How long should a midwife wait after injecting lignocaine before starting an episiotomy repair?

question: What technique helps spread lignocaine evenly along a tear without making multiple skin pricks?

options.B: Fanning the needle while withdrawing and injecting slowly

options.D: Applying hot compresses immediately after the subcutaneous push

question: Which bone landmark is targeted when giving a pudendal nerve block?

question: What is the main advantage of a pudendal nerve block during an assisted vaginal delivery?

question: Which of these is NOT an early warning sign of lignocaine toxicity?

question: What is the specific emergency treatment used for severe heart collapse caused by local anaesthetic toxicity?

question: What type of local anaesthetic is bupivacaine?

question: Why is bupivacaine often chosen for labour epidurals?

question: Which part of the nerve cell does bupivacaine block to stop pain signals?

options.D: Chloride transport proteins

question: How long does bupivacaine typically take to start working after it is given?

question: What vital safety check must a midwife do right before injecting bupivacaine into the perineum?

question: What strength of bupivacaine is usually used for standard perineal numbing?

question: Which pelvic landmark does the midwife feel for internally when giving a pudendal block?

question: What is the main benefit of a pudendal block during a difficult vaginal birth?

question: What is the standard maximum safe dose for plain bupivacaine without adrenaline?

options.D: Fifty milligrams per kilogram

question: Why do pregnant women need lower doses of local anaesthetics?

question: Which of these is NOT an early sign that local anaesthetic is affecting the central nervous system?

question: Which emergency intravenous treatment should be ready when managing severe local anaesthetic toxicity?

question: Why is checking blood pressure regularly essential after a mother receives regional anaesthesia?

question: What postpartum problem should a midwife watch out for after a patient has pelvic floor local anaesthesia?

options.D: Gestational diabetes

question: What is the main benefit of regional anaesthesia compared to general anaesthesia during childbirth?

question: Why must a midwife check baseline maternal and foetal vitals before giving a regional block?

question: Which type of regional block uses a tiny plastic tube left in place for continuous pain relief?

question: Why is a spinal block preferred over an epidural for an emergency Caesarean section that needs to happen immediately?

question: How often should maternal blood pressure be checked immediately after a regional block is given?

question: A woman who just received a spinal block looks pale and says she feels dizzy. What should the midwife do first?

question: What is a frequent side effect of using opioids in regional anaesthesia blocks?

question: Why do women often need a urinary catheter after receiving an epidural block?

question: What happens during a high or total spinal block complication?

options.C: The breathing muscles become weak because the drug reaches the upper chest
options.D: The local anaesthetic completely fails to relieve any labour pain

explanation: When anaesthetic spreads too high, it affects the nerves controlling the diaphragm and chest muscles, slowing normal breathing. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST)?

options.A: Heart rhythm changes
options.B: Passing large amounts of clear urine
options.C: Metallic taste in the mouth
options.D: Sudden muscle twitching or seizures

explanation: Urine output changes are not a sign of LAST; the condition affects the central nervous and cardiovascular systems directly. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of a post-dural puncture headache after a spinal block?

options.A: Too much caffeine consumed before coming to the hospital
options.B: High blood sugar levels during the first stage of labour
options.C: An allergic reaction to the surgical theatre soap
options.D: Leakage of cerebrospinal fluid from the puncture site

explanation: A small hole in the dura lets fluid leak out, lowering pressure around the brain and causing a severe upright headache. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why must a midwife check leg movement before allowing a post-Caesarean mother to walk to the bathroom?

options.A: To confirm the regional block has worn off enough to prevent falls
options.B: To check if her stitches are healing without any wound infection
options.C: To make sure she has not developed a blood clot in her calf
options.D: To test if her kidneys are producing enough waste products

explanation: Remaining numbness and muscle weakness increase the risk of the mother collapsing if she tries to stand up too early. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h6)

question: What main condition is methyldopa used to manage in pregnant women?

options.A: Pregnancy-related anemia
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Gestational hypertension
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Methyldopa is a first-line medication used to manage high blood pressure conditions like chronic or gestational hypertension during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is methyldopa often chosen over other blood pressure drugs in pregnancy?

options.A: It has a long safety record for use during pregnancy
options.B: It requires only a single dose taken just before delivery
options.C: It completely cures chronic hypertension within the first trimester
options.D: It completely prevents the development of pre-eclampsia

explanation: Decades of clinical use provide reassuring safety data regarding fetal development, making clinicians confident in prescribing it to expectant mothers. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which specific receptors does methyldopa stimulate in the brainstem?

options.A: Beta-1 adrenergic receptors
options.B: Angiotensin II receptors
options.C: Muscarinic cholinergic receptors
options.D: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptors

explanation: Methyldopa works centrally by stimulating alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, which lowers activity in the sympathetic nervous system. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does lowering sympathetic nervous system activity help reduce blood pressure?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of circulating blood
options.B: By decreasing peripheral vascular resistance
options.C: By increasing the resting heart rate significantly
options.D: By blocking sodium retention in the renal tubules

explanation: Reducing sympathetic tone relaxes blood vessels throughout the body, lowering the resistance against which the heart pumps and thereby reducing blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h2)

question: At what blood pressure reading is medication usually started during pregnancy?

options.A: 160 over 110 mmHg
options.B: 100 over 60 mmHg
options.C: 120 over 80 mmHg
options.D: 140 over 90 mmHg

explanation: Blood pressure readings consistently exceeding 140 over 90 mmHg generally prompt the start of blood pressure treatment in pregnant women. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks presents with chronic high blood pressure. Which drug is a standard first-line choice?

options.A: Losartan
options.B: Atenolol
options.C: Lisinopril
options.D: Methyldopa

explanation: Methyldopa is a standard first-line oral medication for managing chronic hypertension in pregnant women due to its safety profile. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a typical starting dose for oral methyldopa therapy in pregnancy?

options.A: 250 milligrams
options.B: 1000 milligrams
options.C: 5 milligrams
options.D: 50 milligrams

explanation: Starting at 250 milligrams two to three times daily helps the patient tolerate the medication and minimizes side effects like drowsiness. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is the dose of methyldopa increased gradually over several days?

options.A: To allow time for blood pressure to stabilize and minimize sudden side effects
options.B: To bypass the need for regular antenatal blood pressure checks
options.C: To prevent the drug from accumulating in the amniotic fluid immediately
options.D: To ensure the placenta absorbs all active metabolites all at once

explanation: Gradual titration prevents abrupt drops in blood pressure and helps the patient adjust to side effects like drowsiness. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of methyldopa?

options.A: Dizziness upon standing
options.B: Sudden permanent hair loss
options.C: Dry mouth
options.D: Drowsiness or sedation

explanation: Hair loss is not a recognized side effect of methyldopa, whereas sedation, dry mouth, and dizziness are common. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is periodic liver function testing recommended for patients taking methyldopa long-term?

options.A: To screen for gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: To measure how fast the kidneys filter out excess protein
options.C: To detect rare drug-induced liver injury or enzyme elevations
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the fetus

explanation: Although rare, methyldopa can cause liver irritation, making periodic liver enzyme checks a safe practice during prolonged use. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h5)

question: What common side effect should a midwife warn a patient to expect during the first few days of taking methyldopa?

options.A: Insomnia
options.B: Hyperactivity
options.C: Excessive sweating
options.D: Drowsiness

explanation: Sedation and drowsiness are very common when first starting methyldopa or increasing the dose. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must a midwife advise a patient never to stop taking methyldopa suddenly?

options.A: Stopping suddenly can cause a dangerous rebound spike in blood pressure
options.B: It causes permanent damage to maternal heart valves
options.C: It will immediately trigger preterm labor contractions
options.D: It leads to instant fetal growth restriction

explanation: Abrupt discontinuation of this medication can result in rebound hypertension, putting the mother at risk. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main use of labetalol in pregnancy?

options.A: Lowering blood pressure safely during pregnancy
options.B: Stopping premature contractions in preterm labour
options.C: Preventing postpartum infection after a C-section
options.D: Inducing cervical ripening before formal induction

explanation: Labetalol is commonly used in midwifery to manage high blood pressure disorders like pre-eclampsia without harming the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do midwives prefer labetalol over older blood pressure drugs during pregnancy?

options.A: It lowers blood pressure smoothly while maintaining placental blood flow
options.B: It has zero side effects for either the mother or the developing baby
options.C: It completely cures gestational hypertension within twenty-four hours
options.D: It can be administered exclusively by traditional birth attendants

explanation: Labetalol controls maternal blood pressure gently without cutting off the vital blood supply to the placenta. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which two receptor types does labetalol block to lower blood pressure?

options.A: Beta-1 and muscarinic receptors
options.B: Nicotinic and dopamine receptors
options.C: Alpha-2 and gamma receptors
options.D: Alpha-1 and beta receptors

explanation: Labetalol blocks alpha-1 receptors on blood vessels and beta receptors on the heart to reduce blood pressure effectively. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h2)

question: What happens when labetalol blocks alpha-1 receptors on blood vessels?

options.A: The vessels constrict and blood pressure shoots up
options.B: Heart rate increases rapidly to compensate for volume
options.C: Blood flow to all internal organs completely stops
options.D: The vessels dilate and peripheral resistance decreases

explanation: Blocking alpha-1 receptors relaxes and widens blood vessels so blood flows through more easily. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h2)

question: At what blood pressure reading is labetalol urgently given to prevent a stroke in pregnancy?

options.A: 120/80 mmHg or higher
options.B: 160/110 mmHg or higher
options.C: 100/60 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: Readings of 160/110 mmHg or higher are considered severe hypertension in pregnancy and require urgent treatment. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h3)
